parsed.justification: Rationale A correctly identifies the specific evidence in the comment (Tab. 8, Tab. 2 of supp, MVANet comparison, specific F-beta scores) and accurately applies the rubric, though it notes the justification could be more thorough—which is fair. It grounds its assessment well in the text and avoids unsupported claims. Rationale B also identifies the key evidence correctly and applies the rubric, giving a score of 5. However, B makes an unsupported claim that 'There are no gaps' — this is an assertion not warranted by the evaluation material itself, as the comment does not elaborate on why MVANet is the relevant top-performing model or provide additional context about the comparison. Additionally, B assumes the reference [c] fully substantiates MVANet's results, which is not verified in the evaluation material. Both rationales correctly identify the core evidence, but B's overconfident claim of 'no gaps' weakens its unsupported-claim control.
